Will is jealous when his no-nonsense therapist (guest star Sharon Stone) becomes fast friends with Grace.
Grace convinces Karen to attend her father's (Alan Arkin) birthday party; Karen entertains herself by spending time with Martin's friend Burt (Lee Majors).
Grace's near-death experience prompts her to write her will and jolts Will into making a life-altering career choice.
When Will's writing career fizzles, Malcolm (Alec Baldwin) makes him another job offer; Grace's old college flame (Eric Stoltz) gives her a job decorating his new hotel.
Will becomes suspicious of his new job when he finds himself in an empty office with a German shepherd and a Russian-speaking thug.
Grace contemplates an affair with a married man (Eric Stoltz); Jack begins his new career as a talk-show host; Will continues to hide from Karen the fact that Stan is alive.
When Will suspects that Karen is more upset about Stan being alive than she is letting on, he makes it his mission to help her heal emotionally.
Jack learns that Will has never learned how to swim, so he makes it his mission to teach him.
Jack tells Karen he believes she belongs with Stan, not Malcolm (Alec Baldwin).
Jack brings Baby Glenn (Jason Biggs), who gained notoriety in the '80s after being trapped in a hole for days, to Will's charity auction and carnival.
Grace and Will spot her ex-husband, Leo, on their plane to London; Will charms a pair of gay flight attendants into letting Grace into first-class to talk with Leo.
Jack's decision to move makes Will take a close look at their friendship; Karen and Grace are invited to the memorial celebration for Beverly's (Leslie Jordan) deceased wife.
When Grace finds it impossible to please her mother, Jack offers to help, believing no one knows how to be a good daughter like a gay son.
When the gang spends Christmas at the home of Will's mother, Marilyn Truman (Blythe Danner), Grace gets romantic with Will's brother.
"The Sound of Music Sing-Along" has come to town and no one is more excited than Grace; she plans for her and Will to attend the musical in character-like style by dressing up in costumes.
All of New York society attend Karen's birthday party, but Will, Grace and Jack embarrass themselves and get stuck in the bathroom with the birthday girl.
Will insists that Grace turn down a job offer from his former boss, Margot, who has asked Grace to redecorate the law firm.
Will and Grace dread a dinner date with Rob and Ellen, but the identity of their waiter (Bobby Cannavale) eclipses their friends' big news.
Will, Karen and Grace travel to Los Angeles to support Jack as he accepts an award for Best Local Cable Guy Talk Show Host.
Karen ignores Grace's plea for a low-key wedding and plans a huge affair, hiring Hall & Oates to perform "Maneater" at the ceremony.
Nervous but optimistic Grace decides it is time to tell Leo (Harry Connick Jr.) she is pregnant with his child.
Ecstatic, Jack coerces Will into coming out with him to a cowboy bar to meet his new boyfriend, Travis.
A large corporation takes over OutTV, completely revamping Jack's talk show and giving him a conservative co-host, Britney Spears.
Jack loses his hosting job and vows never to return to acting; Will has a showdown with his father.
At his father's funeral, Will grapples with their last encounter; Grace begins to doubt her potential to be a good mother.
Will and Grace attend childbirth classes; Karen seeks comfort from very busy Jack.
Vince's plans to move into a brownstone with Will do not include Grace; Jack's show premieres.
Will and Grace make a decision about their future together; Jack continues his never-ending search for love; Karen tries to find happiness in Stan's absence.
Will and Grace both falter when their political beliefs are put to the test; Jack and Karen help Will and Grace hide their secret shame from each other, but the truth finally comes out.
Will and Jack try to date younger guys but find it challenging; Grace and Karen experience a crisis that reveals Grace's true feelings about Karen.
Grace finds that the emergency contact called by her doctor's office is ex-husband Leo, not Will; Jack takes on a new job; Karen befriends a 12-year-old girl in the Bronx.
Jack is stunned to learn that his estranged son has a son of his own; Grace and Karen behave badly with the hot new guy at work.
Grace gets a job decorating a string of boutique hotels for an obnoxious hotel mogul; Will is surprised at his reaction to becoming senior partner; Jack owns half of a winning lottery ticket.
Karen has trouble dealing with a personal tragedy; Will, Grace, and Jack try to intervene; Will and Grace's new business relationship begins to show signs of stress.
Will, Grace, Karen and Jack wish they could have experienced Christmas in old New York, but realize the past was not quite as romantic or open to diversity as they pictured it.
Will and Grace try to convince themselves they are okay with dating the same man; Jack and Karen get an annoying commercial jingle stuck in their heads and must seek medical attention.
Will and Grace's old friend Larry decides he's in love with Will; Jack's first day as a Lyft driver doesn't go as planned; Karen tries to help Jack but ends up needing help rather than giving it.
Grace tries to prevent Will from making a scene at his ex-boyfriend's wedding; Jack's wedding hook-up comes with strings attached.
Jack's intimacy issues are challenged by a closeted boyfriend; Will and Grace sell their new line of bedding on live television.

Grace is horrified to realize that she's dated three men from the same family; Will and Karen get on each other's nerves at the office until they bond over watching -- and producing -- their own little telenovela.
A baby shower makes Grace and Will question their life choices; Karen and Jack find a way to combine child labor with musical theater.
Against Jack's advice, Will rekindles a relationship with his first love; Grace reluctantly fights for Karen's civil rights when a bakery refuses to make a cake she wants.
Grace brings Will for support when she goes home to celebrate her deceased mother's birthday; Jack's faith in love is crushed after a breakup; a secret in Karen's marriage is uncovered.
Grace's father and Will's mother end up making a surprising and upsetting connection; Jack rebounds from his breakup with a new love; Karen must decide between her husband and her lover.

Grace's accidental run-in with a curmudgeon she follows on Twitter smacks of romance; Jack makes a terrible impression on Estefan's family after a numbing cream incident; Will helps Karen protect her most prized possession.

After Will and Grace's parents get married, big changes are afoot for the gang: Will gets a teaching job and a beard, Grace decides to run for office, Jack prepares to settle down with Estefan and Karen goes missing.
Jack fears for his grandson's safety at a Texas talent show; Grace and Noah try to have sex.
Now a certified psychic, Jack channels Rosario to help Karen open her heart to love again; Grace learns love means having to say she's sorry.

While on a road trip with her father, Grace reveals a past secret, changing their relationship forever; legendary drag queen Miss Coco Peru emcees a lip sync monologue throw down to determine who will be Jack's best man, Will or Karen.

When Will discovers Noah has a child, he promises to keep the secret from Grace; Karen and Jack's relationship is tested when she fires him from the play she's producing and replaces him with Jon Cryer.

Grace unintentionally meets Noah's daughter Katie; Will's mom Marilyn visits after the death of her beloved dog, but doesn't get the emotional support she expects; Jack argues with his rec center boss, Theo.

In order to land a handsome TV news anchor with a penchant for dim, silly men, Will seeks advice from Jack on how not to be himself; Karen enlists Grace to help get photos of her ex Stan's affair with Lorraine Finster.
Will, Karen and Jack unknowingly take hallucinogens; a client takes up with Grace's sister Janet.
Will and Grace's plan to win over Will's new boss goes awry when he drops dead in their apartment; Estefan and Karen's mutual dislike puts Jack in full damage control mode at his birthday dinner.

Will uses a mock trial in an attempt to repair the rift between Karen and her stepdaughter; Grace and Jack decide to go on a diet together but changing their eating habits proves harder than they thought.
Malcolm enlists Grace to help win back Karen; a workplace flirtation lands Will in hot water.
Will gives newscaster McCoy Whitman another chance; Grace's campaign hits a snag -- her nemesis Val.

Jack's insistence that Will be nicer to Estefan backfires; Grace unknowingly knocks over a prominent figure; when Karen discovers Noah plans to kill off the main character of her favorite romance novel, she forces him to rewrite the story.

After her dad, Martin, is rushed to the hospital, Grace is shocked when he refuses a transfusion of Will's blood; Will's mom, Marilyn, uncharacteristically takes Martin to task; Karen's demands cause Jack to uninvite her to his wedding.
Will and Grace use each other as an excuse to get out of moving in with their boyfriends.
Jack realizes he lost 13 gold coins he's supposed to give Estefan at their wedding to avoid a curse.
Jack and Estefan's destination wedding takes a detour when they're forced to marry at the airport.
Grace returns from her European travels a new woman but soon receives life-changing news.

When Grace admits she's not sure who's the father of her baby, Karen orchestrates a "Mamma Mia" situation with the potential baby daddies; Will worries what will happen if he has a straight son and enlists Jack to help him prepare.

Will discovers a way to finally get back at Jack for years of mocking his hairline; Grace is determined to prove to Mrs. Timmer she's strong enough to handle being a single mother; Karen squares off against Stan's brother in a poker game.
Will and Grace get competitive over whose process of having a baby is more difficult.

In the aftermath of Will and McCoy breaking up, Grace and Jack hire the Grief Panda to help Will process his pain; with Karen completely occupied with her new baseball team, Grace believes that she has to fire Karen to set her free.

Committed to becoming a father on his own, Will meets a potential surrogate who has stellar reviews, but her lifestyle choices give him doubts; Grace pretends to be a former famous Annie to gain entrance into AnnieCon.

Grace and her neighbor give their romance another shot; however, an embarrassing incident puts Grace's relationship, and her dignity, in jeopardy; Will decides it's time for Jack to grow up and cuts him off financially.
Will and Grace set out to prove that their child would be the better candidate for an elite school.
Will and Grace intervene when they discover Grace's niece is dating a bisexual man.

Marilyn goes behind Grace's back to fix her up with a beagle-breeding couple interested in adopting Grace's baby; Will helps Karen deal with a PR nightmare; Jack and Estefan go to extreme lengths to get rid of a mouse.
The gang enters college after graduating from high school; with Mark-Paul Gosselaar, Mario Lopez, Dustin Diamond.
Zack's high-school girlfriend (Tiffani-Amber Thiessen) moves into the same suite as his new love interest (Anne Tremko). With Mark-Paul Gosselaar.
For a cultural anthropology class, Zack (Mark-Paul Gosselaar) tries to find out what women want. With Patrick Fabian.
Zack and Slater (Mark-Paul Gosselaar, Mario Lopez) are invited to join the Sigma Alpha fraternity. With Dustin Diamond.
Slater (Mario Lopez) battles with his feelings when he is challenged to take part in a protest. With Mark-Paul Gosselaar.
The university's most famous alumnus (Charles Grant) makes advances toward Kelly (Tiffani-Amber Thiessen). Guest stars: Gloria Loring, Ed Winter.
Kelly, Leslie and Alex (Tiffani-Amber Thiessen, Anne Tremko, Kiersten Warren) give Mr. Rogers (Bob Golic) some advice about women.
Zack (Mark-Paul Gosselaar) poses as Professor Lasky (Patrick Fabian) to get a date with a fellow student (Brittney Powell).
Zack and Screech (Mark-Paul Gosselaar, Dustin Diamond) fall in love with the same tennis player (Hillary Danner).
Kelly (Tiffani-Amber Thiessen) has a personality change when she works as a waitress. With Mark-Paul Gosselaar.
Zack, Slater, Alex and Kelly (Mark-Paul Gosselaar, Mario Lopez, Kiersten Warren, Tiffani-Amber Thiessen) spend Thanksgiving with underprivileged children.
Kelly and Professor Lasky (Tiffani-Amber Thiessen, Patrick Fabian) discover a mutual attraction.
Kelly (Tiffani-Amber Thiessen) asks Professor Lasky (Patrick Fabian) to her sorority masquerade ball.
Zack, Slater, Alex and Leslie (Mark-Paul Gosselaar, Mario Lopez, Kiersten Warren, Anne Tremko) take an ethics course with a difficult professor (guest star Robert Guillaume).
Zack (Mark-Paul Gosselaar) has a party to raise money for a trip to Cancun, Mexico. With Holland Taylor.
Zack (Mark-Paul Gosselaar) takes a part-time job at the Student Health Center to be close to Kelly (Tiffani-Amber Thiessen).
Each of the students tries to deal with the death of a popular professor. With Mark-Paul Gosselaar and Mario Lopez.
Zack (Mark-Paul Gosselaar) panics at the thought of losing Kelly (Tiffani-Amber Thiessen) and asks her to marry him.
Lisa (guest star Lark Voorhies) visits California University for Kelly's wedding shower. With Tiffani-Amber Thiessen.
Zack's summer romance with an older woman comes to a halt when she discovers he lied to her.
Zack promises to help Screech get a date with Lisa if Screech will do Zack's term paper.
Zack tries to cash in on a stock-market investment to get money to replace his father's video recorder.
A student opposed to killing animals for experiments releases all the science class frogs.
Zack's father falls for Miss Bliss.
Screech finds that an intimidating student has a learning disability.
Zack and a classmate ask the same girl to an upcoming dance, jeopardizing their friendship.
Zack's (Mark-Paul Gosselaar) scheme to get more time to study for a midterm ends up hurting his teacher. With Dennis Haskins.
A student argument helps a teacher resolve a problem with a longtime friend. With Mark-Paul Gosselaar and Dustin Diamond.
A teacher turns a practical joke into a lesson about the criminal justice system. With Mark-Paul Gosselaar and Dustin Diamond.
Zack (Mark-Paul Gosselaar) schemes to steal a kiss from a returning former student who is now a famous rock star.
Zack (Mark-Paul Gosselaar) is offered a chance to join a popular club. With Dustin Diamond.
A retired teacher with unorthodox methods stimulates the class when he substitutes for their regular teacher.
The gang enters a dance contest being held at the Max and hosted by radio personality Casey Kasem. With Mark-Paul Gosselaar and Dustin Diamond.
Lisa's (Lark Voorhies) friends invent ways to pay the bills she has accrued on her father's credit card. With Tiffani-Amber Thiessen and Mark-Paul Gosselaar.
A freak lightning accident enables Screech (Dustin Diamond) to predict the future. With Tiffani-Amber Thiessen and Mario Lopez.
The guys hide a microphone at the girls' party to find out whom Kelly will ask to the dance.
Zack (Mark-Paul Gosselaar) gets into unusual circumstances and clothes when he tries to help Screech (Dustin Diamond) get a date.
Zack's (Mark-Paul Gosselaar) plan to get rid of Slater (Mario Lopez) backfires; Slater's revenge ends up benefiting Screech (Dustin Diamond).
When Ms. Simpson injures her back, a substitute teacher named Tony Crane takes over her class at Bayside; when all the girls fall for Mr. Crane, Zack and Slater become jealous.
When Kelly is nominated as homecoming queen, her dream is shattered as she faces the prospect of winning after she gets a zit; Zack comes up with a solution, but it does not unfold as he plans.
Zack bets against a Valley wrestler named Marvin Nedick that Slater will win his wrestling match against Nedick; things go wrong when Slater decides to quit wrestling.
In order for Kelly to go to a George Michael concert, she has to pass her science test. Zack persuades Screech to tutor Kelly, a ploy which is more for his benefit than for Kelly's.
Zack and his friends form a company selling friendship bracelets for a business class project. He names himself as boss, but Kelly, Jessie, and Slater feel he is treating them poorly.
Everyone is put into pairs for a class assignment to act out married life, so they can be prepared for marriage as adults.
Jessie and Zack (Elizabeth Berkley, Mark-Paul Gosselaar) run for student president, each for different reasons.
Zack's use of a subliminal tape to get Kelly to fall for him has results he never intended.
Zack's (Mark-Paul Gosselaar) schemes to get Kelly (Tiffani-Amber Thiessen) to be his girl land him in detention with a rival for her affections.
The pranks between rival schools Bayside and Valley escalate during the week of the city cheerleading finals.
Screech's (Dustin Diamond) alien disguise is so believable it attracts a government UFO investigator.
Zack (Mark-Paul Gosselaar) decides to throw a surprise birthday party for Screech (Dustin Diamond) in the principal's office.
Slater's (Mario Lopez) pet dies while in Zack's (Mark-Paul Gosselaar) care.
Kelly (Tiffani-Amber Thiessen) chooses to go to the prom with Zack (Mark-Paul Gosselaar); Lisa and Screech (Lark Voorhies, Dustin Diamond) have a "trial" date.
Zack (Mark-Paul Gosselaar) becomes a leader of men when he joins a cadet corps to get out of detention.
The gang uses an old radio station in the school basement to hold a marathon. With Mark-Paul Gosselaar and Dustin Diamond.
Zack's antics get Slater thrown out of driver education classes.
Screech's (Dustin Diamond) house party turns into a disaster when his mother's favorite statue is broken. With Mark-Paul Gosselaar.
Zack (Mark-Paul Gosselaar) tries to cope when he ends up with two dates for the same night; Jessie (Elizabeth Berkley) agrees to a blind date.
Zack has a waiter impersonate his father for a meeting with the principal.
The Miss Bayside Beauty Pageant attracts unusual contestants; Zack and Slater (Mark-Paul Gosselaar, Mario Lopez) make a bet.
Jessie (Elizabeth Berkley) becomes addicted to caffeine pills as she strives to be a perfect student. With Mark-Paul Gosselaar, Tiffani-Amber Thiessen.
Zack's (Mark-Paul Gosselaar) "Girls of Bayside" calendar catches the eye of a fashion photographer. With Dustin Diamond.
Zack's (Mark-Paul Gosselaar) advice line backfires and gets him into trouble with everyone. With Mario Lopez.

Zack makes a surprising discovery about his Native American heritage; Lisa learns her family tree includes a Black American hero of the Underground Railroad; Jessie grapples with guilt over her slave-trading ancestry.
Zack (Mark-Paul Gosselaar) asks Kelly (Tiffani-Amber Thiessen) to go steady and then falls in love with the school nurse.
Mr. Belding's brother Rod (guest star Edward Blatchford) scores points with the class as a substitute history teacher. With Dennis Haskins and Mark-Paul Gosselaar.
Zack (Mark-Paul Gosselaar) plots to reunite Slater (Mario Lopez), Mr. Belding (Dennis Haskins) and himself with their feuding sweethearts.
Some underhanded shenanigans are employed to win a glee club competition.
A costume ball sets the stage for Zack and Kelly (Mark-Paul Gosselaar, Tiffani-Amber Thiessen) to examine their relationship.
Zack (Mark-Paul Gosselaar) has a hard time dealing with the fact that Kelly (Tiffani-Amber Thiessen) has a new boyfriend.
A minor accident sends Zack (Mark-Paul Gosselaar) to the hospital, where he nervously faces the prospect of surgery.
Panic hits when Screech (Dustin Diamond) finds out he has to play a Russian exchange student in the chess finals. With Dennis Haskins.
Zack (Mark-Paul Gosselaar) tries to impress a college girl by lying about his age.
The students adopt a new mascot when a stray ball injures a duck in the pond behind the football field.
Jessie's stepbrother Eric arrives from New York and blackmails her, Zack and Slater (Elizabeth Berkley, Mark-Paul Gosselaar, Mario Lopez).

Jeremy Clarkson, Richard Hammond and James May are challenged to knock down a row of derelict houses in less time than it takes a team of demolition; Jeremy tests an updated version of the classic Jensen Interceptor.
James and Jeremy travel to the British seaside in electric cars; Richard meets the world's top rally team; Lamborghini Aventador.
The Supercar Shootout in Italy with the Lamborghini Aventador, the McLaren MP4-12C and the Noble M6000, guest will.i.am.
China's ever-expanding car industry; NASCAR racing, guest Matt LeBlanc.

Chris, Freddie and Paddy set out to turn an old hearse into the ultimate family car; Chris gets to grips with the lightweight Dallara Stradale; Zara and Mike Tindall go head-to-head in the Reasonably Fast Car.

Paddy and Freddie head to Borneo for a jungle adventure with the Gurkhas, in a pair of very rare, very cheap old cars: Chris Harris tries out the world's most luxurious SUV, the Rolls-Royce Cullinan; Bob Mortimer is the studio guest.

Freddie Flintoff heads to Iceland to compete in the world's maddest motorsport; Paddy McGuinness tries out a Toyota Supra; Chris Harris investigates the story of the Lotus 79, the most beautiful F1 car of all time.
Paddy McGuinness builds his own luxurious off-roader in the shape of the Dirty Rascal; Chris samples the Rolls-Royce Cullinan.
Paddy, Freddie and Chris go on a British summer holiday in super-cheap, second-hand convertibles; Chris tests the new Ariel Atom on track, and Freddie attempts to bungee-jump an old Rover off a dam.

Paddy reveals his ultimate cheap, luxurious off-roader: the home-built "Dirty Rascal;" Chris races the £2.5m McLaren Speedtail against the RAF's newest fighter jet; Romesh Ranganathan is the studio guest.
Paddy, Freddie and Chris are sent on a high-altitude mountain expedition across Peru in second-hand American cars; Chris tests out the latest electric car from Porsche.

Freddie and Chris tackle the toughest off-road race on the planet: the brutal Baja 1000; out on track, there's a showdown between a Renault hot hatch, a Porsche sports car and an old Lamborghini; Laurence and Emilia Fox are studio guests.

Paddy, Freddie and Chris take the latest sports cars from Ferrari, Aston and Porsche on a Yorkshire road trip; on track, Chris tests out Volkswagen's fearsome ID-R electric race; YouTube sensation KSI is studio guest.

Paddy, Freddie and Chris find out if fire, police or ambulance is the fastest of the emergency services; Chris celebrates legendary rally driver Colin McRae; Paddy tests the new BMW M8; Tom Allen is the studio guest.
Testing the Tesla Model 3, Volvo S60 and BMW 3-Series by spending 24 hours in them; Chris heads to Italy to test the Ferrari SF90.
The presenters are ordered to make their cars road legal, and report to a monstrous Wall of Death; the presenters each choose a 200mph legend for a trip.
The cheapest rental cars in Europe are on the island of Cyprus; for just 30 Euros, the crew embark on a series of destructive challenges.
A staycation for Paddy, Freddie and Chris, as they drive British grand tourers on Wales's roads; Chris Harris pays tribute to Sir Stirling Moss and his battles against Ferrari.
An all-electric, all-terrain ice cream van that sweeps streets and has an on-board rubber ring for aquatic delivery.
On location for the production of the "Sweeney" movie, guest Ryan Reynolds.
Mobility scooters that can handle the British countryside, guest Michael Fassbender.
A tribute to Swedish carmaker Saab; Matt Smith in the reasonably priced car.
The chaps are in Donington with three stripped out track cars; guest Alex James.
The guys investigate whether going motor racing is cheaper than playing golf; guest Slash.
Jeremy tries to build a car smaller than the Peel P50; Damian Lewis.
A U.S. road trip in three front-engined supercars that spans Las Vegas to Palm Springs; racing police near the Mexican border.
A Chinese princess offers to adopt Cooper Smith and provide him with a bride.
A British newspaper reporter (Michael Rennie) rides along on the wagon train to observe the Wild West. Brian Keith also guest stars.
Slim and Daisy are invited to Stacey Bishop's wedding, where trouble is expected, since Stacey's ex is determined to stop the nuptials.
Jess tries to help a former outlaw who's trying to go straight, but finds himself drawn into the man's troubles.
Jess searches for Slim, shot and left to die by an outlaw following a robbery, but the captured shooter refuses to talk.
Slim and Jess try to avert bloodshed when they assist neighbors whose ranch has been set afire and from whom horses had been stolen.
Slim goes on the hunt for the shooters after returning to the ranch to find Jess and a stage executive shot.
Outlaws force Dr. Alice McCauley to treat their wounded leader.
Hardie investigates the disappearance of a Wells Fargo agent sent to stake a claim in Oklahoma.
An outlaw gang abducts Jim, who's guarding a payroll, and uses Jim's ID to rob the local Wells Fargo safe.
Following his capture by Hardie, the notorious Johnny Ringo asks to care for his dying sister.
Hardie helps organize the town's citizens to bring good government to the community.
Hardie rides a stagecoach to help protect a valuable gold shipment.
Jim Hardie tries to prove the innocence of a gunslinger who has been framed for a stagecoach robbery and murder.
Hardie guns down an ex-convict.
Hardie looks for the murderer of a man scheduled to receive a reward from Wells Fargo.
A friendly pickpocket helps Hardie bring thieves to justice after they rob his train.
A new school teacher -- also an ex-convict -- becomes suspected of murdering a Wells Fargo agent.
Outlaw relatives complicate the life of Wells Fargo messenger Charles Mason.
Hardie poses as Jesse James while investigating a robbery and murder.
While investigating the robbery of a Wells Fargo office, Hardie witnesses the murder of its agent from the hotel across the street.
Hardie puts trust in newly released outlaw Bill Dowd, but will he regret it?
Bob Dawson is finishing up his memoirs about every man in the territory, and Hardie discovers that some of those men may not want to be found out.
Hardie sets out to solve a 15-year-old mystery about the missing McCray boy.
Attackers strike while Hardie attempts to deliver a golden owl to its wealthy purchaser.
A woman (Beverly Owen) tries to save her sister (Suzanne Pleshette) from a miserable life in a mining town.
Two desperados bring an adolescent sidekick along to a bank robbery.
Cooper learns that his girlfriend Rose's (Annette Funicello) brother is a Brooklyn criminal.
The Bancroft gang robs a family of emigrants of all their possessions.
A woman (Diana Hyland) faces a death sentence after her married boyfriend is found murdered during a cross-country journey. Bradford Dillman also guest stars.
A woman must protect herself and her daughter from a callous man.
A gang joins the train in the guise of farmers and plans to take it over.
While in the desert, Cooper finds a prospector who is lost and near death from exposure and thirst.
Bob Blayne's sons come looking for Jess, bent on revenge because Jess maimed their father years ago; though Jess tries to avoid a shootout, when Slim is injured Jess is forced into action.
Slim investigates when a ranch fight leads to death, but Slim is not convinced the Arapaho chief found with the body is the killer.
Though they don't trust him, Slim and Jess are forced to watch an injured ex-con who was forced to assist in a bank robbery.
A once-prominent Hollywood family discovers a way to improve finances. With John Carradine, Vera Miles, James Farentino.
Professional killers (Jack Cassidy, Harry Townes) with the same employer find that each has the other as his next target.
Only hours before his wedding, a London detective discovers that his American fiancée has disappeared.
A wealthy land developer is shocked to discover that his wife is seeking to divorce him.
A dishonest lawyer takes over a rich widow's holdings but underestimates her companion's (Geraldine Fitzgerald) wrath.
A philandering husband arranges his wife's murder, then has a sudden change of heart and frantically tries to prevent it.
A gruesome surprise awaits a desperate man who thinks that a monkey's paw will bring him financial luck.
A miserly janitor (Oscar Homolka) keeps the contents of a lost wallet, despite the protests of his wife (Jo Van Fleet).
Freed from prison, a thief (Steven Hill) leads his partner (Steve Brodie) to the mine shaft where he hid their loot.
About to be executed for a crime he didn't commit, a man (Harry Guardino) decides to write his side of the story. With Hugh Marlowe.
A teen (Carol Lynley) devises a scheme to escape the influence of her domineering aunt (Jeanette Nolan).
A lonely woman (Dorothy Stickney) believes she has murdered the man (Fred Graham) who killed her cat.
A prosecutor (Pat Hingle) considering a run for Congress is told that he may have convicted an innocent man.
A man (Joseph Cotten) is trapped in an office with the body of his lover (Christine White) whom he just murdered.
A domineering father (John McIntire) tries to run his adult daughter's (Ann Todd) life. With Philip Reed.
A man tries to prove to his friend that a murderer can escape the police if they can't find a motive.
An elderly maid (Mildred Natwick) leaves the parsonage in search of excitement and adventure in Paris.
A physically small husband (Martin Balsam) goes in pursuit of a 200-pound wife-stealing salesman (Leif Erickson). With Norma Crane.
A woman (Jan Sterling) has problems staying away from the racetrack, and it threatens her marriage. With Karl Swenson.
A couple begins their nightly argument when they are suddenly interrupted by a wanted murderer who keeps them hostage.
A soldier (Jacques Bergerac) returning home with a crippled comrade (Marcel Dalio) falls in love with a beautiful girl.
A woman (Jeanette Nolan) questions a man's (Robert Emhardt) motive for wanting to purchase her house.
A woman (Barbara Bel Geddes) falls in love with another man (Michael Rennie) at her engagement party.
A war correspondent's (Gary Merrill) stories about the post-war trail of an Arab leader suddenly change.
A quartet of elderly women (Estelle Winwood, Ellen Corby, Ida Moore, Elizabeth Patterson) try to gain the attention of a handsome detective (Dennis Morgan).
A curious man investigates his tennis partner, only to discover that her supposedly dead husband is very much alive and well.
A meek bookkeeper (John McGiver) is dissatisfied with his dull and boring existence. With Vivian Nathan.
A worrier (James Best) becomes fearful when an old friend (Steve Brodie) shows an interest in his wife (Katharine Bard).
A lawyer (Edmon Ryan) spends Christmas Eve trying to reconcile a feuding brother (Richard Waring) and sister (Carmen Mathews).
A man tries to convince the authorities that he knows who committed the latest murder in a series of strangulations, but no one will listen to him.
A woman (Joanna Moore) learns that a winning sweepstakes ticket is in the suit her former husband was buried in. With Steve Forrest and James Gregory.
A crocodile valise becomes a vital clue in tracking down a murderer (Denholm Elliott).
A bank teller (Robert H. Harris) invents a seemingly foolproof plan to come up with a lot of quick cash. With Jerry Paris and Philip Pine.
While traveling in chauffeured car, a woman (Jessica Tandy) with psychic powers hears a voice telling a tragic love story.
A lawyer, soon to become mayor, extends an invitation to a woman who once accused him of embezzlement.
An old, unemployed actor (Herbert Marshall) uses an even older ploy to get a part in a play. With Tom Helmore and Julia Adams.
A couple (Biff McGuire, Cloris Leachman) on a train promise their son money if he doesn't interrupt a cowboy's (Chill Wills) story.
A morgue attendant becomes hysterical when a practical joker pulls the ultimate prank and pretends to be a corpse.
